applies_to: Trane CGWN water-cooled and CCUN condenserless scroll chillers with CH530 controls, as listed in the BCI2-C integration guide.
summary: The BCI2-C is a non-programmable Trane controller that connects to the CH530 chiller controls over the IPC3 link and serves the chiller data on BACnet MS/TP. This list is the CGWN/CCUN column of the guide's model tables: 62 objects with low instance numbers covering water temperatures, suction and discharge pressures, compressor starts and run times, flow and alarm status. The commands are BO 1 auto/stop, BO 2 diagnostic reset and MO 1 chiller mode.
notes: The guide's tables mark each object against RTWD, RTUD, RTHD, RTAC, CGAM/CXAM and CGWN/CCUN; this file holds the CGWN/CCUN column.
The guide's analog output (setpoint) table has columns only for RTWD, RTAC and CGAM, so no AO setpoint objects are listed for CGWN/CCUN. Check on site whether setpoint objects appear.
The guide's cover names only RTWD, RTAC and CGAM, although its tables include a CGWN/CCUN column; confirm that a BCI2-C (not the older BCI-C) is fitted.
The BCI2-C self-configures, so only the objects that match the connected chiller show up.
The tables have no read/write column: AI/BI/MI are read-only, and the BO/MO objects (listed with relinquish defaults) are the BAS commands, marked writable here.
Units are given as a quantity (Temperature, Pressure, Percent...); SI or I-P follows the BCI2-C Device Units setting. BI 24's active state is printed 'None' in the guide; it means alarm.

source.title: Integration Guide: BACnet Communication Interface for Chillers (BCI2-C)

integration.summary: Address the BCI2-C on the MS/TP trunk and discover it. Write BO 1 auto/stop and MO 1 mode, then read back running state, leaving water temperature and capacity. BI 23 Alarm Present and BI 24 Shutdown Alarm Present are the summary alarms, BI 25 shows the last diagnostic, and BO 2 resets diagnostics remotely.

minimum_points.name: Local Setpoint Control
minimum_points.why: Shows if local setpoints override BAS setpoints

minimum_points.name: Alarm Present
minimum_points.why: Any active alarm on the chiller

integration.enable: BO 1 Chiller Auto Stop Command (Inactive = Stop, Active = Auto; relinquish default True, i.e. Auto) is the BMS auto/stop. BI 1 Run Enabled shows whether the chiller is available to run, and BI 2 Local Setpoint Control shows when the chiller is using local setpoints instead of the BAS setpoints. No BAS setpoint objects are listed for this model.
setup: The BCI2-C is a BACnet MS/TP device only (EIA-485 at 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76,800 bps); the default baud rate is 76,800.

It has no physical rotary dials: the factory address is on a label on the board and is changed in the embedded BCI2 Service Tool (USB, browser at 198.80.18.1) or Tracer TU. Valid MAC addresses are 001-127.
The default software Device ID equals the MAC address; tick 'Use Software Device ID' to set another one. A Tracer SC builds its own device ID from the SC address, link number and MAC.
Communicated units default to SI once the points are created. To switch to I-P, clear the controller with the IPC3 cable unplugged (or the unit powered down) so the Device Units choice unlocks.
For non-Trane front ends, set Max Master (Max Requestor) above the BCI2-C MAC address or the device will not be discovered.
gotchas: The BCI2-C builds its point list from the CH530 controller at first power-up and stores it. If options are added later, clear the controller so it rebuilds the list.
BO 2 Remote Diagnostic Reset Command: after a write of 1 the BCI2-C sends the reset, sets the point back to 0 and clears the priority array. Some diagnostics still need a local reset.

With the external (hard-wired) setpoint option, the chiller follows the external setpoints when the CH530 setpoint source is External/Front Panel, when the setpoint AO is set Out of Service, or when a Tracer SC loses communication with the BCI2-C.
MI 3 MP Communication Status is marked 'Do Not Use This Point' in the document.
